categories.main_business_segments: Kyushu Financial Group operates primarily in three business segments: banking (through Higo Bank and Kagoshima Bank), leasing (via three consolidated subsidiaries), and other financial services (including credit card, DX solutions, payment collection, credit guarantees, securities, and EC mall businesses). The banking segment is the core, providing a wide range of financial products and services. The group also includes regional value co-creation businesses such as digital platforms and e-commerce.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The group leverages advanced banking systems, digital transformation (DX) technologies, and integrated financial platforms. It has invested in digital banking apps, cashless payment solutions, electronic contract services, and AI-driven operational efficiency tools. The group is also developing proprietary systems for CO2 emissions calculation and digital regional platforms.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers are individuals and corporations in the Kyushu region, especially in Kumamoto, Kagoshima, and Miyazaki prefectures. The group serves a broad range of industries, including manufacturing, agriculture, tourism, and local governments, with a focus on supporting regional economic development and SMEs. Retail banking, corporate lending, and regional business support are key markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in the Kyushu region of Japan, particularly Kumamoto, Kagoshima, and Miyazaki, with branch networks extending to Fukuoka, Oita, Nagasaki, Osaka, and Tokyo. The group also supports cross-border business, especially with Taiwan, and has some overseas representative offices.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kyushu Financial Group operates downstream in the financial services supply chain, directly interfacing with end customers (individuals, corporations, and local governments) as a provider of banking, leasing, and related financial solutions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include evolving into a 'regional value co-creation group,' accelerating digital transformation (DX), supporting regional industry growth (notably the semiconductor sector), and advancing sustainability (GX, SDGs, decarbonization, biodiversity). R&D focuses on digital platforms, cashless/payment technologies, AI, and environmental finance solutions. Human capital development and governance enhancement are also emphasized.
categories.revenue_model: The group generates revenue primarily from interest income on loans, fees from financial services (including trust, securities, and insurance products), leasing income, and commissions from credit card and payment services. Additional revenue streams include digital solutions, EC mall operations, and investment advisory services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other regional banks in Kyushu, megabanks, and Japan Post Bank, as well as non-bank financial institutions. The group positions itself as a leading regional financial group with a strong local presence and a focus on regional revitalization and digital innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For FY2025, consolidated ordinary income was ¥251.3 billion, with ordinary profit of ¥42.99 billion and net income attributable to parent shareholders of ¥30.37 billion. Total assets were ¥13.28 trillion, with a workforce of 4,670. The group has shown steady growth in profits and assets, with a strategic goal to further increase profitability and ROE by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kyushu Financial Group differentiates itself through deep regional roots, comprehensive financial services, and a strong commitment to regional economic development. Its unique value lies in combining traditional banking with digital innovation, sustainability initiatives, and tailored solutions for local industries and communities. The group emphasizes co-creation with customers and stakeholders to build a vibrant regional society.
